title: Area architects
goal: I can find the area and the perimeter of rectangles and of shapes made of squares.

learn.intro: Area is the flat space inside a shape. We count squares and write cm². Perimeter is the distance all the way round the edge, in cm.

example.problem: The figure is made of squares with sides of 1 cm. What are its area and its perimeter?
steps: Area: count the squares. 5 + 2 = 7, so the area is 7 cm².
Perimeter: add the sides all the way round. 5 + 1 + 3 + 1 + 2 + 2 = 14 cm.
Check: the figure fits in a box 5 cm by 2 cm. 2 × (5 + 2) = 14 cm.

howto.title: How to find area and perimeter
steps: Area: count the squares, or length × width.
Write cm for the perimeter and cm² for the area.

try.text:
A rectangle is 8 cm long and 3 cm wide.
Its area is {b} cm². Its perimeter is {b} cm.
try.explanation: Area: 8 × 3 = 24 cm². Perimeter: 8 + 3 + 8 + 3 = 22 cm, or 2 × (8 + 3) = 22 cm.

items.text: Every square in the picture has sides of 1 cm. What are the area and the perimeter of each figure?

parts.label: a
parts.text: A: area {b} cm², perimeter {b} cm

parts.label: b
parts.text: B: area {b} cm², perimeter {b} cm

parts.label: c
parts.text: C: area {b} cm², perimeter {b} cm

parts.label: d
parts.text: Same area, different perimeter:   {circ:A,B|A,C|B,C}

items.explanation: Area is the number of squares: A has 8, B has 4 + 2 = 6 and C has 6. Perimeter is the length of the edge: A is 2 × (4 + 2) = 12. B: the box round it is 4 by 2, with a perimeter of 12. The dent in the bottom adds a wall of 1 cm on each side: 12 + 2 = 14. C is 2 × (3 + 2) = 10. B and C have the same area, 6, but different perimeters.

items.text: What are the area and the perimeter of each rectangle?

parts.label: a
parts.text: 8 cm long and 6 cm wide: area {b} cm², perimeter {b} cm

parts.label: b
parts.text: 11 m long and 4 m wide: area {b} m², perimeter {b} m

items.explanation: (a) Area 8 × 6 = 48. Perimeter 2 × (8 + 6) = 28. (b) Area 11 × 4 = 44. Perimeter 2 × (11 + 4) = 30.

items.text: Look at squares.

parts.label: a
parts.text: A square has sides of 7 cm. Its perimeter is {b} cm.

parts.label: b
parts.text: Its area is {b} cm².

parts.label: c
parts.text: A square garden has a fence 36 m long all round. Each side is {b} m.

items.explanation: (a) 4 × 7 = 28. (b) 7 × 7 = 49. (c) The 4 sides are equal, so each is 36 ÷ 4 = 9 cm.

items.text: A rectangle has a perimeter of 30 cm. Its length is 9 cm.

parts.label: a
parts.text: Its width is {b} cm.

parts.label: b
parts.text: Its area is {b} cm².

items.explanation: Length + width is half of the perimeter: 30 ÷ 2 = 15. So the width is 15 - 9 = 6 cm. The area is 9 × 6 = 54 cm².

items.text: A mat is 15 cm long and 9 cm wide. Square tiles with sides of 3 cm cover it exactly.

parts.label: a
parts.text: {b} tiles fit along the length.

parts.label: b
parts.text: {b} tiles fit along the width.

parts.label: c
parts.text: The mat needs {b} tiles in all.

items.explanation: (a) 15 ÷ 3 = 5. (b) 9 ÷ 3 = 3. (c) 5 rows of 3 tiles make 5 × 3 = 15 tiles.

items.text: Mei has 14 cm of wire. She bends all of it into a rectangle. All the sides are whole numbers of cm. List ALL the rectangles.

parts.label: a
parts.text: There are {b} different rectangles.

parts.label: b
parts.text: The one with the greatest area has an area of {b} cm².

items.explanation: Length + width = 14 ÷ 2 = 7. The pairs are 6 and 1 (area 6), 5 and 2 (area 10), 4 and 3 (area 12). That is 3 rectangles. The one closest to a square, 4 by 3, has the greatest area: 12 cm².

items.text: Find the missing sides a and b first. Then find the area, and then the perimeter.

parts.label: a
parts.text: a = {b} cm

parts.label: b
parts.text: b = {b} cm

parts.label: c
parts.text: The area is {b} cm².

parts.label: d
parts.text: The perimeter is {b} cm.

items.explanation: a is the top of the lower part: 8 - 4 = 4 cm. b is the rest of the left height: 6 - 3 = 3 cm. Area: cut into a 4 by 6 rectangle and a 4 by 3 rectangle: 24 + 12 = 36 cm². Perimeter: push the steps out to a box 8 by 6: 2 × (8 + 6) = 28 cm.

items.text: Every square in the picture has sides of 1 cm.

parts.label: a
parts.text: The area is {b} cm².

parts.label: b
parts.text: The perimeter is {b} cm.

parts.label: c
parts.text: Ben fills the gaps to make a 6 by 3 rectangle. He adds {b} squares.

parts.label: d
parts.text: The perimeter of the rectangle is {b} cm.

items.explanation: (a) 6 + 4 + 2 = 12 cm². (b) The staircase has the same perimeter as its box, 6 by 3: 2 × (6 + 3) = 18 cm. (c) The rectangle has 6 × 3 = 18 squares, so he adds 18 - 12 = 6. (d) 18 cm: filling the steps does not change the perimeter.

items.text: Mei draws a rectangle 10 cm long and 2 cm wide. Ben draws a square with the same perimeter.

parts.label: a
parts.text: Each side of Ben’s square is {b} cm.

parts.label: b
parts.text: Whose shape has the greater area?   {circ:Mei’s|Ben’s}

parts.label: c
parts.text: It is greater by {b} cm².

items.explanation: (a) Mei’s perimeter is 2 × (10 + 2) = 24 cm, so Ben’s side is 24 ÷ 4 = 6 cm. (b) Ben’s area is 6 × 6 = 36 cm² and Mei’s area is 10 × 2 = 20 cm². (c) 36 - 20 = 16 cm².

items.text: The figure has a perimeter of 10 cm. Ali adds ONE square at A, B or C.

parts.label: a
parts.text: Which places make the perimeter 12 cm?   {circ:A|B|C}

parts.label: b
parts.text: Which place keeps the perimeter 10 cm?   {circ:A|B|C}

items.explanation: A square that touches the figure along only 1 side adds 2 to the perimeter. A and B each touch 1 side, so the perimeter becomes 12 cm. C fits into the corner and touches 2 sides: it hides 2 cm of the old edge and adds 2 cm, so the perimeter stays 10 cm.

items.text: A square room has a floor area of 64 m².

parts.label: a
parts.text: Each side of the room is {b} m long.

parts.label: b
parts.text: A border goes all round the floor. It is {b} m long.

items.explanation: (a) 8 × 8 = 64, so each side is 8 m. (b) The border is the perimeter: 4 × 8 = 32 m.

items.text: A square has sides of 8 cm. One straight cut makes it into 2 equal rectangles.

parts.label: a
parts.text: Each rectangle has a perimeter of {b} cm.

parts.label: b
parts.text: The 2 rectangles together have a perimeter of {b} cm.

parts.label: c
parts.text: That is {b} cm more than the perimeter of the square.

items.explanation: Each rectangle is 8 cm by 4 cm, so its perimeter is 2 × (8 + 4) = 24 cm. Together: 48 cm. The square’s perimeter is 32 cm, and 48 - 32 = 16. The cut is 8 cm long and it appears on both pieces, so it adds 2 × 8 = 16 cm.
items.hint: Each rectangle is 8 cm by 4 cm. Draw it.

items.text: A rectangle has area 36 cm² and perimeter 26 cm.

parts.label: a
parts.text: Its length is {b} cm.

parts.label: b
parts.text: Its width is {b} cm.

items.explanation: Length + width is 26 ÷ 2 = 13. The pairs that multiply to 36 are 1 and 36, 2 and 18, 3 and 12, 4 and 9, 6 and 6. The pair that adds up to 13 is 4 and 9. Check: area 9 × 4 = 36 and perimeter 2 × 13 = 26.
items.hint: List pairs that multiply to 36. Then add each pair.

items.text: A rectangle is 9 m long and 6 m wide. A rectangle 3 m by 2 m is cut out of one corner, as shown.

parts.label: a
parts.text: The area that is left is {b} m².

parts.label: b
parts.text: The perimeter of the figure is {b} m.

parts.label: c
parts.text: The same piece is cut from the MIDDLE of a long side. The perimeter is then {b} m.

items.explanation: (a) 9 × 6 = 54, and 54 - 6 = 48 m². (b) Cutting a corner does not change the perimeter: 2 × (9 + 6) = 30 m. (c) A notch in the middle of a side takes away 3 m of edge. It adds 3 + 2 + 2 = 7 m of new edge. So the perimeter grows by 4 m: 34 m.
items.hint: Push the corner out. Then think about a notch in the middle.

items.text:
Beyond Level 3: Perimeter patterns.
Squares with sides of 1 cm are joined in a row. 1 square has a perimeter of 4 cm. 2 squares have 6 cm. 3 squares have 8 cm.

parts.label: a
parts.text: A row of 10 squares has a perimeter of {b} cm.

parts.label: b
parts.text: A row with a perimeter of 30 cm has {b} squares.

items.explanation: Each new square adds 2 cm (1 cm on top and 1 cm below). The perimeter is 4 + 2 for every extra square. For 10 squares: 4 + 9 × 2 = 22 cm. For 30 cm: (30 - 4) ÷ 2 = 13 extra squares, so 14 squares.
items.hint: The perimeter goes up by 2 cm for each new square.

items.text:
Beyond Level 3: A path round a pond.
A pond is 6 m long and 4 m wide. A path 1 m wide goes all round the pond.

parts.label: a
parts.text: Pond and path make a rectangle {b} m by {b} m.

parts.label: b
parts.text: The area of the path is {b} m².

items.explanation: The path adds 1 m on each side, so both lengths grow by 2 m: 6 + 2 = 8 and 4 + 2 = 6. The whole rectangle has an area of 8 × 6 = 48 m². The pond has 6 × 4 = 24 m². The path is 48 - 24 = 24 m².
items.hint: Find the area of the whole rectangle. Take away the pond.

items.text:
Beyond Level 3: The largest square tile.
A floor is 12 m long and 10 m wide. It is covered exactly with square tiles of one size. The side of a tile is a whole number of metres.

parts.label: a
parts.text: The largest tile has sides of {b} m.

parts.label: b
parts.text: The floor needs {b} of these tiles.

items.explanation: The side must divide both 12 and 10 exactly. 1 and 2 do. 3 does not divide 10, 4 does not, 5 does not divide 12, and 6 does not divide 10. So the largest side is 2 m. There are 6 tiles along and 5 tiles across: 30 tiles.
items.hint: The tile side must fit exactly in 12 and in 10.

items.text: A rectangle is 9 cm long and 5 cm wide. Its area is {b} cm².
A square has sides of 6 cm. Its perimeter is {b} cm.
Every square has sides of 1 cm. The area is {b} cm². The perimeter is {b} cm.
items.explanation: Area: 3 + 2 + 2 = 7 cm². Perimeter: the figure fits in a 3 by 3 box and has no dents on the outside, so 2 × (3 + 3) = 12 cm.

items.text: A rectangle has a perimeter of 22 cm. Its width is 4 cm. Its length is {b} cm.
items.explanation: Length + width is 22 ÷ 2 = 11. The length is 11 - 4 = 7 cm.
